ev.q: In 2021, 5.9% of adults aged ≥18 years lived in families that were food-insecure in the past 30 days.
The percentage was higher in urban areas (6.2%) compared with rural areas (4.6%) overall
the percentage was similar in rural (22.8%) and urban (20.4%) areas
In 2021, 5.9% of adults aged ≥18 years lived in families that were food-insecure in the past 30 days.
The percentage decreased with family income from 20.8% for those living in families earning <100% of FPL to 2.3%
higher in urban areas (6.2%) compared with rural areas (4.6%) overall and within households earning 100%–199% of FPL
Estimates are based on household interviews of a sample of the civilian, noninstitutionalized U.S. population.

methods_quotes.q: families that reported six or more problems were considered to be food-insecure.
With 95% CIs indicated by error bars.
Urban-rural status is determined by the Office of Management and Budget’s February 2013 delineation of MSAs
